preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] moves forward to the palatal nasal [ɲ] when it is next to a front vowel, a palatal medial or a palatalizing consonant. In Northern Wu, Middle Chinese ŋ- before front vowels and palatal medials became the alveolo-palatal nasal [ɲ] (often written n̠ʲ), while it stayed [ŋ] before back vowels.

examples.note: Before a front vowel the Middle Chinese velar nasal initial became palatal. Hakka keeps ngì /ŋi¹¹/, and Mandarin lost it (yí /i³⁵/).
Before the palatal medial the velar nasal palatalized. Cantonese ngau4 /ŋɐu̯²¹/ keeps [ŋ].

sources: Alkire, T., & Rosen, C. (2010). Romance Languages: A Historical Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511845192
